correctness.rationale: Every coherent adjacency energy eigenvector is a Walsh character. The signed fixed-shell restriction on each exact Walsh weight is evaluated on the full Boolean-lattice harmonic decomposition. A direct Newton finite-difference calculation gives scalar \((-2)^i K_{n-2i,w-i}(r-i)\), with injective harmonic lifts, giving exactly the stated rank for all n,r,w including endpoints. In odd \(n=2m+1\), central polynomial \((1+z)(1-z^2)^{m-i}\) has no internal zero coefficient; other single shells fail row count. In even \(n=2m\), central polynomial \((1-z^2)^{m-i}\) and adjacent \((1+z)^2(1-z^2)^{m-1-i}\) see complementary parity sectors at middle Walsh energy; the latter is injective at every other energy. This proves sharp one- versus two-layer capture. Dissipative semigroup contraction plus positive site losses identify dark states exactly with all-energy trap-vanishing eigenspaces. The bundled checker passed 284 signed restriction ranks, 30 independently built site-basis observability ranks, 8 parity checks and 24 two-shell sector tests. Finite computations only corroborate the all-n proof; no rate claim is inferred.

Moore–Russell supplies Fourier hypercube modes, Varbanov–Krovi–Brun general continuous-time target hitting, Srinivasan and Filmus the general Boolean harmonic framework; those are credited. Published nonbinary all-degree and binary low-degree concentration results do not cover the full exact-energy physical statement. Previous fixed-corner absorption and Hamming-ball absorber classifications have different quantified initial states or trap supports. General Terwilliger machinery may implicitly contain ingredients, and older exact specialization remains a real historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The motivated question is whether a geometrically thin and symmetric absorber support eliminates every coherent dark state, not just a chosen start-state amplitude. The exact all-radius energy profile is an infinite-family structured transport classification. The sharp parity obstruction and its optimal two-layer repair are a nontrivial eigenstate-accessibility boundary: odd central shells asymptotically occupy only \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) of vertices yet capture all initial states, whereas even central shells retain exponentially many dark modes. The result offers a reproducible, exact benchmark for dissipative quantum-network controllability. It does not claim optimization over arbitrary individual traps or finite-time relaxation speed.
